title: What happened in AI — Nov 8, 2026
intro: Builders are shrinking their agent stacks: Lovable deleted most of its agent code and one engineer dropped all agent skills, citing Anthropic's 80%+ Claude Code prompt cut with no measurable eval loss.
The infrastructure gap is memory: every coding tool stores it differently, and several projects propose a shared format or an inspectable store.
highlights: Lovable deleted almost all its agent code after 100k PRs.
Anthropic reportedly cut over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt with no measurable eval loss.
Agent memory lacks a shared format; the OpenTelemetry analogy is gaining ground.
ARTEX-driven campaigns stole 190k gaming credentials for under $400 in model costs.
Uncensored models in agent loops: most fail about half of multi-step tasks.

categories.name: Agent harnesses: less scaffolding, more deletion
categories.summary: Builders report pruning agent code and skills as models improve, and the lighter harnesses they keep are small and inspectable.

articles.title: Lovable: we deleted almost all our agent code

articles.title: Author deletes all their agent skills

articles.summary: A 25-year programmer describes a local agent setup and says LLMs in agent harnesses became capable of full features in January 2026.

categories.name: Agent memory and context become shared infrastructure
categories.summary: Memory is fragmented per tool, and new projects try a shared format or an inspectable filesystem-style store.

articles.title: Agent memory needs its OpenTelemetry moment
articles.summary: Each coding tool stores memory in its own shape and none can read the others; the post surveys existing formats and sketches a shared spec.

articles.title: OpenViking: a context database for agents
articles.summary: Open-source store that exposes knowledge, memory and skills as a viking:// virtual filesystem agents navigate with ls, tree, read and grep.

articles.title: RepoMagpie: your coding agent remembers repos you've tried
articles.summary: Keeps your verdicts on libraries, CLIs and MCP servers so the agent checks them before installing a tool you already ruled out.

articles.title: Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin
articles.summary: Splits work in two: Elephant keeps project context and drafts the spec; Goldfish reviewers read it without the prior conversation to expose blind spots.

articles.title: aiport: a local LLM gateway
articles.summary: Go gateway that routes Claude Code, Codex, Ollama and cloud models through one endpoint and shows which app called what.
